chunks: And from him (Al-Hadith) from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil from Mihran who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the mukatab (a slave who has contracted to pay a sum for his freedom) who dies and leaves children. He said: 'If it was stipulated upon him (the father) that his children would remain slaves, then his children are slaves. And if it was not stipulated upon him, his children will strive to free their father, and they will be freed if they pay (the debt).'

key_terms.الْمُكَاتَبِ: A slave who has entered into a contract with his master to pay a specific sum of money in installments in exchange for his freedom.
key_terms.مَمَالِيكُ: Plural of mamluk, meaning slaves or bondsmen.

ai.seo_question: What happens to the children of a slave who has contracted for his freedom (mukatab) when he dies?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the inheritance of manumission status for the children of a *mukatab* (slave with a contract for freedom) upon the father's death, distinguishing between cases where the contract explicitly bound the offspring versus those where they retain the right to redeem themselves. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that contractual stipulations (*shart*) dictate the legal standing of heirs in manumission contexts, ensuring that the children are not automatically enslaved unless agreed upon. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Islamic law to balance the master's financial rights with the potential for the family's complete emancipation through the children's efforts.
